rationales.deterministic-orchestration-v2: form (c), with (a) and (b) also firing. The contributed system is a code framework (§5.1: 'We implemented a framework... it constructs the prompts and provides input to the LLM through its API, runs the system adaptation loop with constraint verification, and activates the feedback loop by presenting feedback to the LLM with a constraint violation report'). This is the canonical form (c) case from §3 verbatim: a code loop that calls a model to generate an artifact (the LLM is dispatched for one bounded job — generate/repair the adaptation manager), runs it inside the adaptation loop, and feeds the code's OWN verification result back to the model for repair. The LLM is a component, not a controller — it never decides what runs next. form (a): the sequence generate→execute→verify→(accept | append report & regenerate) is fixed in code; the harness advances the state and the model cannot skip the verifier. form (b): the consequence of the verifier's outcome is code-fixed — §3.4/§5.2 'A candidate AM is accepted only if it passes all checks across the suite of test runs,' a failing check triggers a code-driven retry, and §5.2 fixes a code-enforced abort at 'a maximum of 10 unsuccessful iterations.' Preconditions: (1) orchestrator is the framework code, not AI — the generated AM's own runtime ensemble-resolution decisions sit INSIDE the artifact being verified, not in the outer control flow; (2) a model performs a step (LLM synthesizes the AM); (3) top level — the feedback loop IS the outermost flow of the contributed system, and §1.1 stresses it is 'fully automated' with 'no human code inspection,' so no human/agent advances it.
